newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Max to sell stake in Norseman Gold.
newsitem.headline: Max to sell stake in Norseman Gold.

text.p: Max Resources NL said on Monday it had entered into an agreement with Australasian Gold Mine NL (AGM) to sell its interest in the Norseman gold project.
Max will sell half its current tenement holdings in the project for the issue of five million AGM ordinary shares. It is expected those share will be issued in August.
The purchase was completed by AGM along with the completion of a capital raising which included the issue of fully paid ordinary AGM shares at A$0.50 per share.
AGM's capital raising indicates a value of A$2.5 million for the sale consideration, which exceeds the value Max's directors had placed on the asset, the company said.

On completion of a bankable feasibility study and the signing of bank finance to pay for mining of the Norseman area, AGM will acquire the remaining 50 percent of Max's interest in this project for a further payment of A$2 million.
That payment becomes due only if the feasibility study is positive.

If the A$2 million payment is not made by June 30, 1998, AGM is pay Max 15 percent interest. AGM has to acquire the final 50 percent of Max's Norseman interest by June 30, 1999 or the right to acquire it lapses.
Max retains an option to convert the final A$2 million payment into equity in AGM at the of A$0.75 per share in lieu of being paid cash.
If a takeover offer is made for AGM, the A$2 million payment becomes due immediately.
